questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The relative basic strength of the compounds is correctly shown in the option.
questions.solution:
The correct order of relative basic strength will be
$\ddot{\mathrm{NH}_3 > \ddot{\mathrm{NH}_2-\ddot{\mathrm{NH}_2 > \ddot{\mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{OH}$
In $\mathrm{NH}_3$, the lone pair is completely available for donation, hence is most basic whereas $\mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$ and $\mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{OH}$ can be considered as derivatives of $\mathrm{NH}_3$. Here, $\mathrm{H}$ is replaced by $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ forming $\mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2$ and $-\mathrm{OH}$ forming $\mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{OH}$ being highly electron withdrawing due to $-\mathrm{O}$ will decrease the election density most on $-\mathrm{N}$.
$\therefore$ Least basic elect;on withdrawing $-I$-effect of
$-\mathrm{NH}_2$ is less as compared to - $\mathrm{OH}$.
Hence correct order of basic strength is
$\mathrm{NH}_3 > \mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{NH}_2 > \mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{OH}$

questions.q: Arrange the following in decreasing order of their boiling points.
questions.solution: The boiling point of $(\mathrm{A})$ alcohol is highest due to $\mathrm{H}$-bonding. Out of primary (B), secondary (D) and tertiary amines (C), the boiling point in decreasing order is Primary amine > Secondary amine > Tertiary amine as intermolecular association decreases in same order, being highest in primary amine and least in tertiary amine due to steric hindrance. $\therefore$ The correct decreasing order of boiling point in given compound is A > B > D > C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following bases in decreasing order of basicity is
(i) Aniline
(ii) O - nitroaniline
(iii) m-& nitroaniline
(iv) p& - nitroaniline
questions.solution:
Basicity is directly proportional to the $+ M, + I$ effect, but it is inversely proportional to the $- M, - I$ effect. Aniline is the highest basic because it does not have any group. But the nitro group can show the $- I$and $- M$ effect. The nitro group at meta position show only the $- I$ effect. But at ortho and para position, it will show the $- M, - I$ effect both. So, the $m -$nitroaniline is more basic than the $p -$nitroaniline and $o -$nitroaniline.

So, the basicity order is :-

Hence, the decreasing order of basicity is $( i ) >( iii )>( iv )>( ii )$.

questions.q:
Which of the following statement about aniline is false?
A. Aniline is a strong base than ammonia.
B. Aniline is a less basic than methylamine.
C. $\mathrm{p})$ K_b\) of aniline is more than that of ammonia.
D. Aniline reacts with bromine water to form a white precipitate.
questions.solution: $According to Lewis theory, the species which easily loses a pair of electron is Lewis base, lone pair on nitrogen in aniline are involved in resonance with the benzene ring and therefore not available for donation to that extent as in \mathrm{NH}_{3}$. Since, ammonia can lose easily electron pair while aniline cannot, thus ammonia is a stronger base than aniline.Thus, statement (A) is false. Hence, the correct option is (a).
